header: Formatted body copy at a readable measure
bodytext:
This is the block an editor writes into. Whatever the rich text editor allows — subheadings, lists, links, emphasis — arrives here with the page's own rhythm already applied, and the column stops at seventy characters so no line runs wider than the eye can track back.

Headings inside start one level down

The block's own title is the heading above. Anything the editor adds inside sits below it, so a long page keeps one readable outline instead of a flat run of equal-weight titles.

  • Lists take the body scale and their own indent
  • Links carry the accent colour and an offset underline
  • Emphasis is the theme's semibold weight, never a second typeface

Nothing here is styled by the element itself: the shared prose rule does the work, which is why one theme switch reaches this paragraph and every other one at the same time.
